title: Regrouping an ordered tower of adjoint comparisons
statement:
Let $r\geq0$, let $\mathcal C_0,\ldots,\mathcal C_r$ be categories, and for $0\leq i\leq j\leq r$ let $P_{ij}:\mathcal C_j\to\mathcal C_i$ have right adjoint $G_{ij}$, and let $F_{ij}:\mathcal C_i\to\mathcal C_j$ be another functor. Use identity functors and identity adjunctions when $i=j$. Suppose natural isomorphisms $\alpha_{ijk}:P_{ij}P_{jk}\cong P_{ik}$ and $\phi_{ijk}:F_{ik}\cong F_{jk}F_{ij}$ are given, satisfying the associativity pentagons and unit equations. Let $c_{ijk}:G_{ik}\cong G_{jk}G_{ij}$ be the adjunction conjugate of $\alpha_{ijk}$, using the composite adjunction whose counit is $\varepsilon_{ij}\circ P_{ij}(\varepsilon_{jk})$. Adjunction, composite adjunction and conjugation have the meanings of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. For each $i<r$ choose a natural transformation $\eta_i:F_{i,i+1}\to G_{i,i+1}$. Define $\Gamma_{ii}=1$ and recursively
$$\Gamma_{i,j+1,K}=c_{i,j,j+1,K}^{-1}\circ\eta_{j,G_{ij}K}\circ F_{j,j+1}(\Gamma_{ij,K})\circ\phi_{i,j,j+1,K}.$$
Then the $c$ satisfy their associativity pentagon and identity equations, every $\Gamma_{ij}$ is natural, and for every $i\leq j\leq k\leq r$ and $K\in\mathcal C_i$,
$$\Gamma_{ik,K}=c_{ijk,K}^{-1}\circ\Gamma_{jk,G_{ij}K}\circ F_{jk}(\Gamma_{ij,K})\circ\phi_{ijk,K}.$$
In particular every parenthesization of a fixed ordered list of the $\eta_i$ gives the same transformation under these specified comparisons. No transformation is assumed invertible, and no permutation of the ordered list is asserted.

proof.text:
First transfer the specified coherence, rather than choosing new right-adjoint comparisons. Fix $i\leq j\leq k\leq l$. The assumed left-comparison equation is
$$\alpha_{ikl}\circ(\alpha_{ijk}P_{kl})=\alpha_{ijl}\circ(P_{ij}\alpha_{jkl}).$$
Apply conjugation between $P_{il}\dashv G_{il}$ and the triple composite adjunction. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], conjugation reverses vertical composition. Clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], with identity non-adjoint sides and an identity square in the unchanged factor, says that the conjugates of $\alpha_{ijk}P_{kl}$ and $P_{ij}\alpha_{jkl}$ are respectively $G_{kl}(c_{ijk})$ and $c_{jkl}G_{ij}$. Thus the conjugated equality is
$$G_{kl}(c_{ijk})\circ c_{ikl}=(c_{jkl}G_{ij})\circ c_{ijl}. \tag{C}$$
The two triple composite adjunctions used here agree under the canonical functor associator: their Hom bijections are the same three successive bijections of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], merely parenthesized differently. Their associator components on objects and arrows are identities. Hence this calculation also includes the canonical associators, rather than presupposing an extra coherence theorem. For a repeated adjacent index the corresponding left comparator is the specified unitor, and the identity-adjunction Hom bijection is the identity. Conjugation of this identity is the identity by clause 4 of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. This proves all right-comparison unit equations as well as (C).

proof.text: Every $c_{ijk}$ is a natural isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Naturality of $\Gamma$ follows by induction on the interval length: $\Gamma_{ii}$ is the identity transformation, and the recursive expression is a composite of $\phi$, a functor applied to a natural transformation, a component of the natural transformation $\eta_j$ at $G_{ij}(-)$, and $c^{-1}$. For a map $u:K\to K'$, the four naturality squares compose to the naturality square for this expression; applying $F_{j,j+1}$ to the inductive square preserves its equality. The unit equations imply $\Gamma_{i,i+1}=\eta_i$, since the recurrence with $j=i$ has only identity comparisons and $\Gamma_{ii}=1$.

source.place: Proof Step 2 (ordered reassociation only); detailed agent-written mate calculation and induction, using Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean, mateEquiv_hcomp and conjugateEquiv_comp

proof.text:
We prove the displayed block identity for all $i\leq j\leq k$ by induction on $k-j$, uniformly in $i,j$ and the input object. When $k=j$, its right side reduces to $\Gamma_{ij}$ by $\Gamma_{jj}=1$, functoriality of the identity functor and the unit comparisons proved in Step 1. If $i=j$ the assertion likewise reduces to $\Gamma_{jk}$, so repeated-index cases are included. For the successor step put $l=k+1$, $H=F_{kl}$, $J=G_{kl}$, $A=\Gamma_{ij,K}$ and $b=\Gamma_{jk}$. Substitute the inductive formula for $\Gamma_{ik,K}$ into the recurrence for $\Gamma_{il,K}$, and distribute $H$ over composition. This gives, with composition read right to left,
$$\Gamma_{il,K}=c_{ikl,K}^{-1}\eta_{k,G_{ik}K}\,H(c_{ijk,K}^{-1})\,H(b_{G_{ij}K})\,HF_{jk}(A)\,H(\phi_{ijk,K})\,\phi_{ikl,K}. \tag{E}$$
All factors are typed using $A:F_{ij}K\to G_{ij}K$ and $b_M:F_{jk}M\to G_{jk}M$; in particular the next naturality substitution involves a morphism in $\mathcal C_k$.

source.place: Proof Step 2 (ordered reassociation only); detailed agent-written mate calculation and induction, using Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Mates.lean, mateEquiv_hcomp and conjugateEquiv_comp

proof.text:
In (E) use naturality of $\eta_k:H\to J$ on $c_{ijk,K}^{-1}:G_{jk}G_{ij}K\to G_{ik}K$:
$$\eta_{k,G_{ik}K}H(c_{ijk,K}^{-1})=J(c_{ijk,K}^{-1})\eta_{k,G_{jk}G_{ij}K}.$$
Invert (C) from Step 1 to obtain
$$c_{ikl,K}^{-1}J(c_{ijk,K}^{-1})=c_{ijl,K}^{-1}c_{jkl,G_{ij}K}^{-1}.$$
The assumed $F$-coherence and then naturality of $\phi_{jkl}$ on $A$ give respectively
$$H(\phi_{ijk,K})\phi_{ikl,K}=\phi_{jkl,F_{ij}K}\phi_{ijl,K},\qquad HF_{jk}(A)\phi_{jkl,F_{ij}K}=\phi_{jkl,G_{ij}K}F_{jl}(A).$$
Replacing these three adjacent substrings in (E), associativity of morphism composition yields
$$\Gamma_{il,K}=c_{ijl,K}^{-1}\bigl(c_{jkl,G_{ij}K}^{-1}\eta_{k,G_{jk}G_{ij}K}H(b_{G_{ij}K})\phi_{jkl,G_{ij}K}\bigr)F_{jl}(A)\phi_{ijl,K}.$$
The parenthesized factor is exactly the defining recurrence for $\Gamma_{jl,G_{ij}K}$. This is the required block identity for $(i,j,l)$ and completes the induction. The only adjunction-coherence input to this computation was (C), obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]; all remaining substitutions are the displayed naturality equations, functoriality and the assumed $F$-coherence.

Finally induct on the number of leaves in a binary parenthesization of a fixed consecutive interval. A single leaf evaluates to $\eta_i=\Gamma_{i,i+1}$ by Step 2; the empty interval evaluates to the identity. At the root of any larger tree there is a cut $j$ of its interval $[i,k]$. By induction its subtrees evaluate to $\Gamma_{ij}$ and $\Gamma_{jk}$. The root operation is precisely $c_{ijk}^{-1}(\Gamma_{jk}G_{ij})F_{jk}(\Gamma_{ij})\phi_{ijk}$, which the block identity of Steps 3--4 identifies with $\Gamma_{ik}$. Thus every such tree has the same value. This is an induction on the actual evaluation of trees and needs no theorem asserting that rotations connect parenthesizations. For $r=0$ only the empty interval occurs. No cancellation or inversion of an $\eta_i$ or a $\Gamma_{ij}$ has been used.

lean.statement: theorem orderedAdjointTower_regrouping (r : ℕ) (C : Fin (r + 1) → Type u) [∀ i : Fin (r + 1), Category.{v} (C i)] (T : OrderedAdjointTowerData r C) (eta : ∀ j : Fin r, T.F j.castSucc j.succ (Nat.le_succ _) ⟶ T.G j.castSucc j.succ (Nat.le_succ _)) : (∀ (i j k l : Fin (r + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) (hkl : k ≤ l) (X : C i), (T.comparison i k l (hij.trans hjk) hkl).hom.app X ≫ (T.G k l hkl).map ((T.comparison i j k hij hjk).hom.app X) = (T.comparison i j l hij (hjk.trans hkl)).hom.app X ≫ (T.comparison j k l hjk hkl).hom.app ((T.G i j hij).obj X)) ∧ (∀ (i k : Fin (r + 1)) (h : i ≤ k), T.comparison i i k le_rfl h = (T.G i k h).leftUnitor.symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerRight (eqToIso (T.G_id i)).symm (T.G i k h)) ∧ (∀ (i k : Fin (r + 1)) (h : i ≤ k), T.comparison i k k h le_rfl = (T.G i k h).rightUnitor.symm ≪≫ isoWhiskerLeft (T.G i k h) (eqToIso (T.G_id k)).symm) ∧ (∀ (i j : Fin (r + 1)) (h : i ≤ j) (X Y : C i) (f : X ⟶ Y), (T.F i j h).map f ≫ (T.gamma eta j i h).app Y = (T.gamma eta j i h).app X ≫ (T.G i j h).map f) ∧ (∀ (i j k : Fin (r + 1)) (hij : i ≤ j) (hjk : j ≤ k) (X : C i), (T.gamma eta k i (hij.trans hjk)).app X = (T.phi i j k hij hjk).hom.app X ≫ (T.F j k hjk).map ((T.gamma eta j i hij).app X) ≫ (T.gamma eta k j hjk).app ((T.G i j hij).obj X) ≫ (T.comparison i j k hij hjk).inv.app X) ∧ (∀ (i j : Fin (r + 1)) (h : i ≤ j) (tree : OrderedAdjointTowerTree r i j h), tree.eval T eta = T.gamma eta j i h)
